## 固定收益市場主線

美國債市10月13日恢復交易，長天期公債上漲。紐約聯準銀行總裁John Williams提出的貨幣緊縮展望，比市場定價所反映的路徑溫和，10年期殖利率下降2.94個基點至5.2084%，30年期下降3.87個基點至5.5569%。他仍認為今年適合再升息一次，但若經濟依其預測發展，目前看來2027年不必再升息。

這波回升集中在較長天期，並非所有期限殖利率同步下滑。2年期殖利率收盤略升，信用市場則走弱：美國投資級利差小幅擴大，高收益利差明顯擴大。能源價格偏高，加上政府與科技企業同時爭取借款資金，仍牽制公債行情。IMF新提出的主權再融資警告、騰訊近$57億的發債，以及Skydance債券進一步下跌，分別呈現這些融資壓力；Williams的判斷則幫助市場從稍早的弱勢中回穩。

## Williams縮小升息展望，長天期公債回升

週一美國銀行假日過後，週二是公債市場自上週五以來的首個交易日。Williams接受訪問之前，長債已獲買盤支持。Bloomberg報導，美國交易時段早盤一筆長債期貨大宗交易，似乎進一步帶動行情。道明證券的Gennadiy Goldberg表示，許多投資人認為，從較長投資期間來看，當前利率頗具吸引力。市場也預期財政部官員可能減少長天期公債供給，為這些債券增添支撐。

Williams的談話改變了盤中的政策討論。2年期殖利率回吐稍早一度達3個基點的升幅，收在4.789%，僅較前次債市收盤上升0.21個基點。5年期下降1.44個基點至5.0013%。2年與10年期利差收窄3.15個基點至41.94個基點，2年與30年期利差收窄4.08個基點至76.79個基點，延續較長天期債券相對受到青睞的走勢。

過去一週的回升已較為明顯，但仍未扭轉一個月來融資成本上升的趨勢。10年期殖利率較10月6日下降7.31個基點，卻仍較9月11日高24.04個基點；30年期相對這兩個基準，分別下降10.3與上升20.29個基點。週二10年期殖利率的降幅主要來自實質殖利率，後者下降2.36個基點至2.8615%；損益兩平通膨率僅下降0.58個基點至2.3469%。過去一個月，實質殖利率上升26.55個基點，損益兩平通膨率反而下降2.51個基點，因此主要變化仍是實質借款成本提高。

Williams是FOMC永久投票成員，也是委員會副主席。他表示，目前展望仍支持今年再升息一次，並預期明年通膨將接近2%目標。聯邦基金利率期貨則仍反映12月升息、2027年再升兩次。他的看法降低了市場對持續多次緊縮的預期，但未撤回對下一次升息的支持。

這項區分有其具體理由。Williams指出，關稅大致如預期推高進口商品價格，卻未出現他原先擔憂的更廣泛價格效應。短期更棘手的是能源：先前期待伊朗衝突解決、油價回落，結果過於樂觀；原油與成品燃料價格的差距擴大，又增加了一波通膨衝擊。這些變化促使他明確支持9月升息。

AI投資則帶來另一股需求。他提到，晶片及相關商品價格突然上漲，使用這些零組件的消費產品也受影響，營建勞動成本亦有上升跡象。若需求依其預期發展，AI產業的供給可能需要超過未來兩年的時間才能跟上。不過，他對通膨放緩的預測，不以這種失衡立即消失為前提，而是認為經濟其他部分受到貨幣政策約束、關稅效應淡化，以及生產力提高，將使總需求與總供給大致維持平衡。

他援引的依據包括通膨預期仍受錨定、薪酬成長溫和，以及單位勞動成本符合2%或更低通膨的水準。紐約聯準銀行的基礎通膨指標約為2.3%，達拉斯聯準銀行截尾平均指標在過去六個月也處於相近水準。他未見勞動市場全面過熱，整體成長僅略高於其潛在成長估計。國民所得帳修正後，他小幅上調對基礎成長的評估，反映供給面與需求面都更強。

這項判斷仍取決於能源與AI以外的通膨如何演變。Williams表示，對週三即將公布的核心CPI，沒有某個特定數字會決定他的反應。他估計實質中性利率約為1%或略高，中性利率較先前上升約0.25至0.5個百分點。若其預測實現，明年經濟將距離中性狀態不遠。

聯準會理事Christopher Waller週二稍早在新德里提出另一個角度。他說，長期殖利率上升正在抑制住宅、汽車及其他利率敏感需求，加強貨幣緊縮的效果。AI投資則可能先推高物價兩、三年，生產力效益才會更廣泛顯現。推動AI建設的買方對價格相對不敏感，競相購買半導體，也把漲價傳導給其他使用者。

Waller同時區分殖利率上升的原因：若來自更強的成長，相較於通膨疑慮或法國等地的財政擔憂，情況較有利。他表示，美國標售需求尚未顯示，對財政赤字的焦慮正迫使聯準會調整政策以協助政府融資。在他看來，成長與資金流入為美國提供一定保護，但更高的借款成本已影響民間決策。

波士頓聯準銀行總裁Susan Collins的預先準備講稿，據報於週一發表、週二見報，帶來另一項政策訊號。她預期年底前利率還會略升，是否需要升息及其時間則取決於後續數據。她的基本展望是成長持續、就業接近充分，效率提升逐步讓通膨回到2%；但她認為另兩種較不利情境的可能性幾乎相當：一是AI投資熱潮蔓延至家庭支出，使勞動市場過熱；二是關稅與能源壓力持續，尤其伊朗戰爭若延續。她關注的是通膨是否仍集中在少數領域，或擴散至其他類別。

週二的活動數據呈現好壞參半的經濟，而非全面疲弱。9月NFIB小型企業樂觀指數由98.7降至97.9，略低於市場預估98。ADP每週就業變動由23,750人增至24,750人；截至10月10日當週，Redbook銷售年增率由8.6%升至10.4%。企業信心雖轉弱，就業與零售觀察卻未顯示需求突然崩落。

9月成屋銷售四個月來首次上升，月增1.5%，年率達399萬戶，高於市場預估395萬戶。8月銷售年率修正為393萬戶，月減幅修正為3.2%。不過，美國全國房地產經紀人協會首席經濟學家Lawrence Yun表示，8月與9月仍是今年銷售最慢的兩個月份。9月部分交屋發生在房貸利率隨後升至7.49%之前；融資變貴後，他也觀察到更多合約延後成交。

房價中位數年增1.3%至$41萬7,500。待售屋存量增加4.6%至160萬戶，相當於4.8個月供給。南部與西部銷售均增加2.8%，中西部持平，東北部下降。已完成交易略有回升，但許多買方安排購屋後，負擔能力所受的限制又進一步加劇。

Williams發言後，美股從盤中低點回升。標普500收盤僅跌0.02%，報7,805.45；Nasdaq 100下跌0.31%，半導體股下跌0.23%。美元指數下降0.36%至102.215。原油帶來的緩解較少：WTI上漲0.97%至每桶$94.65，Brent下跌0.37%至$106.26。長債上漲是在能源仍昂貴的環境下維持，而非燃料成本明確反轉後的結果。

## 騰訊完成大額發債，AI融資更趨挑剔

騰訊週二完成的融資規模，高於前一天提出的約$50億發行計畫。知情人士表示，公司定價發行人民幣260億元、約合$38.8億的境外人民幣債，以及$18億美元債。這是騰訊自2020年以來最大規模的境外債券發行；截至紐約時間上午11時，美元債訂單超過$74億，香港下午較晚時，人民幣債需求超過人民幣1,050億元。

發行金額與訂單顯示，即使AI相關估值承壓，大型且獲利的科技借款人仍能吸引大量資金。募集資金將用於一般企業用途，包括主要以購買晶片為主的AI資本支出。騰訊先前已表示，投資將維持高檔至2027年。

AirTrunk取得股權資金則較困難。知情人士表示，這家由Blackstone支持的資料中心營運商，因利率上升與波動削弱需求，將原訂$15億的新加坡REIT上市延至明年。公司曾考慮把發售殖利率由先前的5.5%提高至約6%，規模與時間仍在討論。Firmus取消澳洲IPO後，這次延期再添一項融資挫折；即使擬提高分配收益，仍未能化解投資人對未來獲利及其他利率投資選擇的疑慮。

美國銀行最新基金經理人調查顯示，投資人對同一投資循環仍有相當大的曝險。加碼科技股的比例由前月30%升至37%，為2020年8月以來最高。45%預期2027年會出現AI泡沫，42%則不認同。Broadcom執行長Hock Tan另批評，一些不了解所投資企業的投資人抱持過度期待。這些疑慮伴隨週二亞洲晶片股重挫，韓國股市一度跌逾7%；其後美國半導體股的跌勢才收斂。

爭取債券資金的競爭不只涉及科技業。Bloomberg一項新的比較指出，Amazon與Alphabet自7月以來已發行約$700億等值債務；新興市場主權國際債券發行額卻從去年同期$910億降至$450億。其中，投資級新興市場發債減少56%至$290億，10月至今尚無發行。過去半年，新興市場美元債平均殖利率上升近1個百分點，達2025年4月以來最高。

美國銀行的Merveille Paja警告，評等相近的科技借款人可能排擠投資級主權發行人，此時高油價與較高政策利率也正收緊融資條件。開發中國家年底前約有$277億美元與歐元外債到期，其中沙烏地阿拉伯為$52億，土耳其為$30億。對即將償還到期債務的借款人而言，等待融資變便宜的代價，與為擴張投資而發債的企業不同。

Vanguard的Micah James表示，部分利差最窄的投資級主權債已出現壓力，因為投資人更容易以科技債替代。Allianz的Eoghan McDonagh則描述反向資金流：美國投資帳戶一直買進高品質新興市場主權債，以分散對超大型雲端業者的曝險。這場競爭在各評等與國家並不一致；主權債的風險溢酬與分散投資價值，可能抵銷部分高獲利企業借款人的吸引力。

Rishi Sunak在新德里論壇提出前瞻性的規模比較，預測2027年科技企業在超過10年期債務上的淨發行量，可能大於美國政府。融資需求正在延伸至債券、專案貸款與設備融資架構，民間投資因而與本已龐大的公共借款並存，而非取而代之。

新研究也說明這波建設對產業的影響。由Alicia Garcia-Herrero領導的Natixis經濟學家，在週一報告估計，全球AI資料中心用電需求將於未來五年倍增。中國占全球電力設備出口的比重，從2017年的22%升至去年的33%，該產業也出現企業重新增加資本支出的跡象。這項研究指出，除了開發前沿模型的企業，供應運算所需實體基礎設施的業者也可能受益。

IMF週二公布的《世界經濟展望》將AI視為正向需求衝擊，但效益至今集中在相對少數經濟體，尚未帶動廣泛生產力提升。IMF小幅上調2026年全球成長預測至3.1%，2027年維持3.4%，並警告，一旦市場重估預期獲利與生產力，這股支撐可能驟然結束。能源庫存消耗也縮小了各經濟體承受持續供應干擾的空間。

## 主權再融資風險延伸至銀行、附買回與退休基金

IMF最新《全球金融穩定報告》將政府公債殖利率上升列為金融體系最大的新增威脅。資本市場部門副主任Athanasios Vamvakidis表示，殖利率飆升是相較4月評估最明顯的變化。眼前的憂慮不只是通膨，而是高債務、較短期限及更昂貴再融資的組合。

IMF官員Jason Wu表示，債務規模更大、期限更短，使展期風險提高；對價格敏感的投資人，包括利用銀行槓桿的避險基金，也占有更大比重。借款人若須頻繁重返市場，這些特徵可能使財政或通膨衝擊更難被吸收。IMF對AI修正風險的評估，與六個月前大致相同：極強的獲利緩和了估值壓力，但整個生態系的槓桿已增加。韓國與日本是股市曝險最直接的市場之一。

法國監理機關的最新評估，則顯示當地銀行承受主權風險的能力。ACPR週二報告，法國銀行2025年持有約€1,900億本國公共債務，占其主權證券24%、總資產2%。秘書長Emmanuelle Assouan表示，曝險有限且分散，讓監理機關對近期利差變化的影響感到放心；法國銀行持有的本國政府債務，也少於若干歐洲同業。

ACPR未見法國銀行適用任何主權降評自動觸發條款。不過，Bloomberg Intelligence分析師表示，主權評等若遭負面調整，可能對銀行發行人與債券評等造成壓力。監理機關的資產負債表評估與評等疑慮，涉及不同管道：前者是直接持有部位與即時承受能力，後者則是國家信用惡化如何影響銀行的融資信用地位。

IMF對英國財政的評估較為正面，前提是持續整頓。它預期赤字由今年GDP的3.8%降至2031年的1.4%，為G7預估降幅最大者。總債務占GDP比率則由今年102%升至2027年的102.5%，再降至2031年的100.2%。另以淨債務計算，8月為93.8%，低於先前官方預測約100%。

名目產出回溯上修，以及通膨支撐稅收，部分解釋了較佳的起點。Oxford Economics的Andrew Goodwin提醒，歷屆政府陸續縮減緊縮力度，預期路徑仍是債務先升再趨平。IMF呼籲財政大臣John Healey，生活成本補助應有針對性且屬暫時措施，避免普遍燃料補貼、全面減稅與價格管制，因為這些措施成本高且難以撤除。

IMF將英國2026年成長預測由1%上調至1.3%，2027年則由1.3%下調至1.2%。今年3.3%、明年2.8%的通膨預測，以荷莫茲海峽於3月重新開放、其後10月恢復正常為假設。較高長期利率預期將抑制消費與投資。

Ray Dalio週二發文提出更悲觀的美國融資評估。他估計，美國政府今年須展期約$10兆債務，並新增$2.1兆借款；現有持有人即使只小幅減少再投資，也可能形成龐大缺口。他也認為，日本殖利率上升、支持日圓的誘因，可能促使日本投資人將約$1.1兆美國公債持倉中的部分資金匯回。這是對日後可能出現供需惡性循環的警告，與週二支持長債回升的買盤形成對照。

Harley Bassman指出另一項技術性弱點。殖利率上升使較長天期證券成為公債期貨最便宜可交割債券時，期貨合約的存續期間與負凸性都會增加。經理人若希望抵銷這些曝險，可能在到期日接近時賣出其他長債，放大既有跌勢。Bassman表示，負凸性已達上次於2007年出現的水準。他估計，20年期殖利率若超過6%，可能引發相當於$1,100億標售規模的賣盤；他所描述的殖利率當時約為5.6%。

新公布的ICMA調查呈現2026年上半年歐洲擔保融資如何調整。6月，人工經紀商占未到期附買回交易的比重達16.2%，較六個月前提高約2.5個百分點，為2012年以來最高；電子系統占比降至24.3%，為16年低點。60家受訪機構6月10日的附買回與反向附買回交易總額，達創紀錄的€14.92兆，較12月增加9.3%。

報告作者Richard Comotto表示，經紀商能拆分大型交易、尋找對手方，減少資訊外洩，對不規則期限或較難處理的擔保品尤其有用。BrokerTec的Sara Carter表示，市場波動促使參與者將融資期限縮短至每日交易，以便迅速解除部位。調查期間雖有波動與量化緊縮，附買回利率整體仍穩定。英國避險基金出售的長天期英國公債部位，大多由實錢投資人承接，降低了這些部位的附買回融資需求。這份歷史調查記錄的是取得流動性的方式改變，而非週二新增的融資利率衝擊。

智利退休金監理機關披露，美國利率反轉造成更大的後果。七家民營AFP退休基金持有的外國利率衍生性商品，由一年前獲利$14億，轉為截至9月虧損$77億。這些基金管理約$2,290億資產，建立了美國利率下降時可受益的收取固定利率交換部位。11月4日生效的新衍生性商品風險限制，要求進一步解除部位，但殖利率上升已使合約平倉更昂貴。

Citigroup估計，截至4月，每1個基點殖利率變動的曝險已達約$1.31億，2024年初則為$1,060萬。合約名目本金由接近$7,000億的高峰，降至8月約$5,250億。監理機關表示，超額持倉已有相當部分完成調整，但尚須解除的規模不明。多數收取固定利率部位由保守型E基金持有，這類基金今年平均損失10.4%，其中9月損失4.9%；C與D基金當月分別損失3.1%與4.2%。曝險下降之際，剩餘交易的退出成本仍在提高。

## 能源成本居高，亞洲政策訊號分歧

日本最新生產者物價數據，降低了日本央行立即再升息的急迫性。9月企業商品物價年增6.8%，較7.6%放緩，月減0.3%，與8月降幅相同。農林漁業價格年減13.3%，主要由米價帶動；石油與煤炭價格漲幅在補貼協助下降至11.5%。投入成本仍高，但漲勢正放緩。

熟悉日本央行想法的人士表示，官員傾向在10月30日會議避免連續升息，若數據支持，12月仍可行動。央行9月已將利率升至1.25%。週二隔夜交換定價顯示，10月升息機率約10%，截至12月升息機率為88%；若通膨上行風險突然升高，10月最終決策仍保留彈性。

總裁植田和男週二在國會表示，任務是將基礎通膨穩定在2%左右。官員編製季度展望時，將評估先前緊縮、高油價及待實施的暫時食品消費稅減稅的影響。自7月底預測以來，油價已上升約15%。因此，生產者物價放緩支持央行多留時間評估政策，卻未消除日本面臨的進口成本壓力。

澳洲新公布的9月會議紀錄顯示，央行不願再等，因而將利率升至4.6%。8月識別的多項上行風險已實現或正在累積，理事會認為，等待確認可能代價高昂。若全球中性利率已上升，先前4.35%的利率是否足以恢復平衡，也受到質疑。海外相對利率路徑則透過匯率與進口通膨影響決策。

會議紀錄承認，讓通膨回到2%至3%目標與維持就業之間的取捨正在惡化。持續的不利供給衝擊，可能需要需求與就業成長放慢。支持維持利率的理由，主要是超出預期的下行風險，包括房價下跌可能比原先假設更嚴重地削弱家庭支出。房價已回到一年前水準、信心也惡化，理事會仍選擇在需求明顯受抑之際因應通膨。

韓國央行總裁申鉉松週二表示，在官員確信通膨會及時回到目標之前，政策將維持限制性。他樂見韓元進一步升值，認為有助家庭購買力與國內經濟。7月與8月升息後，基準利率為3%；隨著效果更明朗，後續緊縮擬逐步推進。

IMF將韓國2026年成長預測上調0.7個百分點至3.3%，與韓國央行預測一致，2027年也上調至2.8%。9月出口逾倍增至創紀錄的$1,209億，半導體出口增加263%。通膨由8月3.1%降至2.9%，但仍高於2%目標。申鉉松表示，AI需求足以抵銷戰爭對成長的拖累，且兩者合力加重價格壓力。他也說，央行六個月政策點陣圖若要檢討，將先累積至少一年的使用經驗，於明年或更晚進行，目前未訂時間表。

英國央行外部委員Megan Greene以IMF上調成長預測及勞動市場韌性為由，認為3.75%的政策利率還不夠具限制性。近月她支持升息0.25個百分點至4%，但在九人貨幣政策委員會中仍屬少數。她警告，反覆供給衝擊可能影響薪資與價格預期；若央行未落實投資人已反映的升息，市場預期的緊縮可能逆轉。

Bellway業績則呈現住宅需求的限制。建商預期截至2027年7月的年度交屋量為9,000至9,400戶，低於9,695戶，平均售價約持平於£32萬5,000。經調整營業利益率降至10.1%，稅前獲利£2億7,020萬，未達預期。財務長Shane Doherty表示，首次購屋者約6%的利率正在壓抑需求。公司計畫回購£1.5億股票，仍與銷量展望轉弱並存。

捷克數據提供另一項通膨擴散跡象。9月核心通膨達3.1%，高於央行預測2.9%，市場服務與商品價格均略加速。整體通膨升至2.5%，主因燃料，食品價格下跌的抵銷效果則較先前減弱。官員已表示，11月5日將在維持與升息之間選擇；央行預期整體通膨於2027年初將暫時超過3%。

巴西經濟學家的利率預測走向相反方向，通膨展望卻惡化。央行每週調查將年底Selic利率預測由13.50%降至13.25%，目前為13.75%；年底通膨預測則由5.01%上調至5.22%。投資人預期總統挑戰者Flavio Bolsonaro將推動較緊財政。10月25日第二輪投票前，週二BTG Pactual／Nexus民調顯示，他占有效票52%，Lula為48%，誤差為2個百分點。較低的利率預測反映了投資人對未來財政緊縮的期待。

## 信用損失凸顯併購與重整風險

Skydance收購Warner Bros. Discovery後，投資人重新評估其獲利能力，債券週二再跌。2036年到期、票息9.125%的債券下跌約2.5美分，至每1美元面額91美分，9月30日發行價則為100。2033年到期、票息7.55%的投資級債券，風險溢酬由上週五2.87個百分點擴大至2.95個百分點，發行時為2.375個百分點。五年期違約保護成本由上週五5.132個百分點升至5.728個百分點。

JPMorgan週二研究量化了這筆交易對新券表現的影響。截至10月8日的十天，新發行投資級債券落後該行較廣泛指數27個基點，是疫情以來最大差距；若排除Skydance，新券反而領先約4個基點。損失集中於單一發行人，有助解釋為何整體新券表現不佳，其他交易卻仍有穩健需求。該行將弱勢與發行量不如預期連結，儘管基金流入強勁、利率波動降低。

Altice International債權人10月13日將資產移轉爭議訴諸法院。包括Arini、Diameter、Elliott、Silver Point、King Street、Sona與Invesco的團體，在紐約州法院提告，指控控股股東Patrick Drahi參與多年安排，將價值移至債權人無法追索之處。訴狀指出，約$54億公司間貸款被移至無須對原告所持債務負責的Altice Luxembourg；另有貸款流向持有Drahi之BT股權的實體，其出售收益據指未償還Altice International。

債權人也質疑2025年11月移轉葡萄牙與多明尼加業務，指這兩項業務占調整後EBITDA近80%。公司淨債務約€80億，自2027年起陸續到期；去年新增€7.5億債務，並創造再借€20億的空間。訴訟接續上週談判，可能使不利於既有債權人團體的後續融資更複雜。Altice與債權人均拒絕評論。

塞內加爾希望年底前取得IMF計畫並達成債務減免協議，但出現具體障礙。知情人士表示，負債的國際審計尚未完成，年底前取得IMF董事會批准因此困難。包括BlackRock、VR Capital與Farallon的債券持有人團體在10月3日信函警告，若要求本金減記或降低平均票息，可能造成重大延誤。

該團體建議，將國際債券期限延長至擬議IMF計畫結束之後，不減少名目本金或降低平均票息，並主張這樣可以符合與官方債權人待遇可比性的要求。所需減免程度將由IMF債務可持續性分析決定。塞內加爾希望與官方及民間貸款人同步談判，擬排除非洲金融共同體法郎債務，以及$17億銀行總報酬交換，也都是達成協議須處理的議題。

政府10月6日簡報列出，2025年底債務為$484億，占重新計算基期後GDP的105%，其中外債$328億。欠商業債權人$97億，雙邊貸款人$78億。2033年與2048年到期債券週二交易價略高於每1美元面額52美分，回吐簡報後部分漲幅。新的審計障礙與債權人提案，使12月達成協議、2027年第一季實施的可行路徑更為受限。

烏干達將政策回應提前，召開週三特別會議，不再等到11月12日。先令週二一度跌至每美元4,224，坎帕拉下午較晚時回升至4,135；自8月25日以來已貶約10%。9月通膨達4.6%，為三年多來最高，政策利率自上次會議以來維持9.75%。經濟學家Ronald Ochen預期央行將升息因應匯率壓力。此前已有投資人撤資，總統也反對出售外匯存底。

新報導披露新世界9月底機場物業協議的更多融資條件。機場管理局將接手HK$180億的11 Skies綜合項目，並免除數十億港元租金，新世界則提供HK$30億現金與服務。機管局可於三年內以HK$22.5億，向鄭氏家族投資公司買入7.5億股、約30%股權，價格約較目前股價低43%。

選擇權要求家族維持最大股東地位，因此行使之前，需要新增資本或擴大股本基礎。知情人士表示，鄭氏家族近期曾考慮Bain可能入股，但總體經濟不確定性使雙方轉趨審慎。公司有近$110億債務最早自明年起到期，並已宣布就約$9.91億的2027年與2028年債券進行換債。協議爭取了時間、減輕負債，股權條件則影響下一步資本決策。

BP的資產負債表呈現相反方向的改善。第三季末淨債務由6月$223億，降至約$135億至$145億，提前達到2027年底目標區間。煉油利潤率略低於每桶$47，天然氣交易獲利顯著高於第二季，石油交易則大致持平。公司同時揭露$30億至$45億減損，主要來自能源轉型業務。能源供應干擾強化煉油與交易現金創造能力，也暴露投資組合其他部分的損失。

銀行業績呈現高利率環境下另一種分歧。客戶持續借款，JPMorgan、Citi與Wells Fargo的放貸收入創下新的季度紀錄。利率與利差商品交易轉弱，外匯與商品較有韌性；在週二公布業績的大型銀行中，Citi是固定收益收入下降趨勢的例外。JPMorgan股票交易收入年增49%。五家大型銀行前九個月股票收入可望超過$660億，比預估債券、外匯及商品收入高約$30億；總額仍含對週三公布業績銀行的估計。

週二紐約時間下午5時之後公布的信函中，聯準會理事Lisa Cook的律師表示，她因歐洲公務會議，無法出席11月5日白宮聽證，要求改在12月8日至9日FOMC會議之後。Cook否認房貸詐欺指控，認為是為免職找藉口。律師也質疑調查委員會的客觀性，援引Kevin Hassett曾公開暗示有理由將她免職。

另一則較晚的KKR報導提出亞洲信用估值看法。Dengzhao Pan指出，高品質借款人資產負債表更強，預期信用損失較低。亞洲投資級美元債平均殖利率5.8%，今年下跌約1.4%，美國同類債券下跌2.5%，平均存續期間分別為4.6與6.4年。亞洲利差較6月初低點高15個基點，卻仍較2025年底窄2個基點。這項比較區分了較高整體殖利率，與幅度小得多的信用風險補償變化。

## 後續市場觀察

美國9月CPI將於紐約時間10月14日上午8時30分公布，是Williams所強調政策區分的下一項直接檢驗。市場預估整體通膨月增0.6%，前值0.4%；年增3.6%，前值3.4%。核心通膨預估月增0.2%，前值0.3%；年增2.5%，前值2.4%。燃料通膨加速、基礎價格漲勢放緩，與服務及非能源商品壓力全面擴大，所帶來的政策問題不同。這也是10月27日至28日FOMC會議前最後一次CPI公布。

週三《褐皮書》將補上各地企業評估。週四公布9月PPI，預估增加0.5%，前值0.4%；零售銷售預估增加0.3%，前值1.2%；首次申請失業救濟人數預估20萬，前值19萬7,000。週五工業生產預估增加0.4%，前值持平。這些觀察將共同顯示，在AI相關需求仍強之際，住宅市場所見的抑制效果是否正變得更廣泛。

新加坡週三決策將更早檢驗亞洲政策。Bloomberg調查的20名經濟學家中，17名預期匯率政策區間斜率提高，三名預期不變。8月核心通膨2.2%，為兩年高點，支持進一步緊縮；第三季成長預估5.1%，則意味成長放慢。公共運輸票價預定12月上漲7%，美國銀行預期能源費用本季下降後，明年將反彈。重點是成長放緩時進口通膨的持續性，而非傳統政策利率決策。

烏干達緊急會議將顯示，央行如何回應匯率再探極端水準。韓國10月22日決策與日本10月30日會議，面對的是科技需求與進口成本不同程度的組合。英國10月28日預算，將讓IMF財政整頓評估與Greene對需求及通膨的憂慮同場對照。匈牙利預計下週提出的財政計畫，將提供朝歐元趨同目標前進的下一批具體數字，而不只是再次宣示長期目標。

融資考驗日益取決於個別發行人。塞內加爾須完成負債審計並就減免條款達成協議，才能維持年底時程；智利退休基金在付出高昂成本減少部位後，還須面對11月4日衍生性商品限制。Skydance後續交易與營運進展，也將影響新券市場，近期表現落後異常集中在這個借款人。另一方面，荷莫茲海峽周邊船舶再遭攻擊，德國與烏克蘭反對只限煉油廠的能源休戰，使實體燃料供應與停止攻擊的範圍仍未明朗。這些情況仍影響週三數據背後的通膨展望，也攸關在殖利率仍高時進行再融資的借款人。

long_thesis.english_markdown:
## Opening Fixed-Income Thesis

Long-dated Treasuries rallied as U.S. bond trading resumed on October 13, with Federal Reserve Bank of New York President John Williams giving investors a less demanding outlook for monetary tightening than the one priced into markets. The 10-year yield fell 2.94 basis points to 5.2084% and the 30-year declined 3.87 basis points to 5.5569%. Williams still considers another increase appropriate this year, but currently sees no need to raise rates again in 2027 if the economy follows his forecast.

The recovery favored longer maturities rather than producing a uniform fall in yields. The two-year finished marginally higher, while credit weakened: U.S. investment-grade spreads widened modestly and high-yield spreads widened noticeably. Expensive energy and the competing demands of government and technology borrowing remained important counterweights to the Treasury rally. Fresh IMF warnings about sovereign refinancing, Tencent's almost $5.7 billion bond sale and further losses in Skydance debt showed different parts of that financing pressure, even as Williams' assessment helped markets recover from earlier weakness.

## Williams Limits His Tightening Outlook as Long Bonds Recover

Tuesday was the Treasury market's first session since Friday, following Monday's U.S. bank holiday. Longer bonds were already finding support before Williams' interview, with Bloomberg reporting an early U.S. block trade in long-bond futures that appeared to reinforce the move. TD Securities' Gennadiy Goldberg said many investors regarded prevailing rates as attractive over a longer horizon. Speculation that Treasury officials might reduce long-maturity supply also supported those securities, although that remained an expectation about a future financing decision.

Williams' remarks then changed the intraday policy conversation. Two-year yields erased an earlier increase of as much as 3 basis points. At the end of the session, the two-year stood at 4.789%, up just 0.21 basis point from the previous bond-market close. The five-year fell 1.44 basis points to 5.0013%. The 2s10s curve narrowed 3.15 basis points to 41.94, and 2s30s contracted 4.08 to 76.79, extending the preference for longer duration.

The recovery has become more substantial over the week without reversing the monthly rise in financing costs. The 10-year yield was down 7.31 basis points from October 6 but still 24.04 above September 11; the corresponding 30-year changes were a decline of 10.3 and an increase of 20.29 basis points. At 10 years, Tuesday's move came mainly from the inflation-adjusted yield, which fell 2.36 basis points to 2.8615%. Breakeven inflation declined a smaller 0.58 basis point to 2.3469%. Over the month, real yields rose 26.55 basis points while breakevens fell 2.51, leaving higher real borrowing costs as the dominant change.

Williams, a permanent FOMC voter and the committee's vice chair, said his current outlook remained consistent with another increase this year and inflation approaching the 2% target next year. Federal funds futures, by contrast, continued to anticipate a December increase followed by two more in 2027. His view therefore reduced the perceived need for an extended tightening sequence without withdrawing support for the next move.

He supplied a detailed explanation for that distinction. Tariffs had raised imported-goods prices largely as expected, without producing the broader price effects he had feared. Energy was more troublesome in the near term: earlier hopes for a resolution of the Iran conflict and falling oil prices had proved too optimistic, while a widening gap between crude and refined-fuel prices added another inflation shock. Those changes helped persuade him to firmly support September's rate increase.

AI investment provided a separate demand impulse. Williams described abrupt increases in chip and related goods prices, including consumer products using those components, as well as signs of higher construction labor costs. He expects supply within the AI sector to take longer than the next two years to catch up if demand develops as he anticipates. His disinflation forecast does not depend on that imbalance disappearing immediately. Instead, he expects monetary restraint elsewhere in the economy, fading tariff effects and stronger productivity to keep aggregate demand and supply broadly balanced.

The evidence he cited included anchored inflation expectations, subdued compensation growth and unit labor costs consistent with inflation of 2% or less. The New York Fed's underlying inflation measure was around 2.3%, with the Dallas Fed trimmed mean around a similar level over the previous six months. Williams saw no broad labor-market overheating and described overall growth as only a little above his estimate of potential. National-account revisions had led him to lift his assessment of underlying growth modestly, reflecting a stronger supply side as well as demand.

That assessment remains conditional on the evolution of inflation outside energy and AI. Williams said he had no particular core CPI number that would determine his response to Wednesday's release. He also put the real neutral interest rate at about 1% or a little higher, with neutral having risen roughly 0.25-0.5 percentage point from its earlier level. The economy would not be far from neutral next year if his forecast materializes.

Governor Christopher Waller offered another perspective earlier Tuesday in New Delhi. Higher long-term yields were restraining housing, automobiles and other interest-sensitive demand, he said, adding to the effects of monetary tightening. He also warned that AI investment could push up prices for two or three years before its productivity benefits became more widely apparent. Buyers pursuing the buildout were relatively insensitive to prices, bidding up semiconductors and transmitting those increases to other users.

Waller distinguished the sources of higher yields. An increase associated with stronger growth was more favorable than one driven by inflation fears or fiscal concerns, such as those surrounding France. He said U.S. auction demand had not shown fiscal-deficit anxiety forcing the Fed to adjust policy to help finance the government. Growth and capital inflows offered the U.S. some protection, in his assessment, even as higher borrowing costs were already affecting private decisions.

Boston Fed President Susan Collins supplied a separate policy signal in prepared remarks described as delivered Monday and reported Tuesday. She expected rates to rise somewhat further before year-end, with the need and timing dependent on incoming data. Her central outlook combined continued growth, near-full employment and efficiency gains that gradually returned inflation to 2%. But she regarded two less favorable scenarios as almost as likely: an AI investment boom spreading into household spending and labor-market overheating, or persistent tariff and energy pressure, particularly if the Iran war continued. Her emphasis was on whether inflation remained concentrated or broadened into other categories.

Tuesday's activity releases presented a mixed, rather than uniformly weak, economy. September NFIB business optimism fell to 97.9 from 98.7, just below the 98 consensus. Weekly ADP employment change increased to 24,750 from 23,750. Redbook's year-on-year sales reading for the week of October 10 rose to 10.4% from 8.6%. The employment and retail observations accompanied weaker business confidence without indicating a sudden collapse in demand.

Existing-home sales rose for the first time in four months, increasing 1.5% to an annualized 3.99 million in September. That exceeded the 3.95 million consensus and followed a revised 3.93 million pace and a revised 3.2% monthly decline in August. National Association of Realtors chief economist Lawrence Yun nevertheless said August and September were the year's two slowest months. Some September closings preceded the subsequent jump in mortgage rates to 7.49%, and Yun reported more contract delays as financing became more expensive.

The median price increased 1.3% from a year earlier to $417,500. Inventory rose 4.6% to 1.6 million homes, equivalent to 4.8 months of supply, while sales increased 2.8% in both the South and West, were flat in the Midwest and fell in the Northeast. The release showed a modest recovery in completed transactions alongside an affordability constraint that had intensified since many of those purchases were arranged.

Equities recovered from session lows after Williams spoke. The S&P 500 finished down only 0.02% at 7,805.45, while the Nasdaq 100 fell 0.31% and semiconductor shares lost 0.23%. The Dollar Index declined 0.36% to 102.215. Oil offered less relief: WTI rose 0.97% to $94.65 a barrel, while Brent slipped 0.37% to $106.26. The long-bond gains thus survived a still-expensive energy backdrop rather than following a decisive reversal in fuel costs.

## Tencent Clears a Large Sale as AI Financing Becomes More Selective

Tencent completed a larger financing than the roughly $5 billion offering it had outlined a day earlier. The company priced 26 billion yuan, or $3.88 billion, of offshore yuan bonds and $1.8 billion of dollar securities Tuesday, according to people familiar with the transaction. Its largest offshore note sale since 2020 drew more than $7.4 billion of dollar orders by 11 a.m. New York time and more than 105 billion yuan of yuan demand by late afternoon in Hong Kong.

The completed amounts and order books establish that a major, profitable technology borrower could still attract substantial funding despite the pressure on AI-related valuations. Proceeds are intended for general corporate purposes including AI capital spending, chiefly chip purchases. Tencent had already indicated that investment would remain elevated into 2027; the new development was the execution and scale of the financing, not a fresh expansion of the spending plan.

Equity capital was harder to obtain at AirTrunk. The Blackstone-backed data-center operator is delaying a planned $1.5 billion Singapore REIT listing until next year because higher rates and volatility have weakened demand, people familiar with the plans said. It had considered increasing the offered yield to about 6% from an earlier 5.5%. Size and timing remain under discussion. The postponement adds a new funding setback after Firmus's abandoned Australian IPO, with the higher proposed payout still insufficient to settle investor concerns about future earnings and competing interest rates.

Bank of America's latest fund-manager survey showed how much exposure remained tied to the same investment cycle. The share overweight technology rose to 37% from 30% the previous month, its highest since August 2020. Some 45% expected an AI bubble in 2027, while 42% did not. Broadcom chief executive Hock Tan separately criticized extreme expectations among investors unfamiliar with the businesses they were financing. Those concerns accompanied Tuesday's sharp Asian chip-stock losses, including a decline of more than 7% in South Korean shares at one point, before the U.S. semiconductor selloff moderated.

The competition for bond capital extends beyond technology. A new Bloomberg comparison showed Amazon and Alphabet had issued about $70 billion-equivalent of debt since July, while emerging-market sovereign eurobond issuance had fallen to $45 billion from $91 billion over the comparable period a year earlier. Investment-grade EM issuance declined 56% to $29 billion, with no sales so far in October. Average yields on EM dollar bonds had risen almost a percentage point during the half-year to their highest since April 2025.

Bank of America's Merveille Paja warned that similarly rated technology borrowers could crowd out investment-grade sovereigns just as expensive oil and higher policy rates tightened financing conditions. Developing countries have about $27.7 billion of dollar and euro external debt maturing by year-end, including $5.2 billion for Saudi Arabia and $3 billion for Turkey. Waiting for cheaper funding therefore carries a different cost for borrowers with approaching maturities than for companies issuing to expand investment.

Vanguard's Micah James said some pressure had already emerged among the tightest-spread investment-grade sovereigns, where investors could more readily substitute technology debt. Allianz's Eoghan McDonagh described a counterflow: U.S. accounts had been buying high-quality EM sovereigns to diversify their hyperscaler exposure. The distinction matters because the contest is not uniform across ratings and countries. A sovereign's risk premium and its diversification value can offset some of the appeal of a highly profitable corporate borrower.

Rishi Sunak added a prospective scale comparison at the New Delhi forum, forecasting that technology companies could become larger net issuers of debt with maturities above 10 years than the U.S. government in 2027. That is his forecast about next year's long-duration supply. It arrives as financing demand expands into bonds, project loans and equipment structures, placing private investment alongside already-large public borrowing rather than replacing it.

New research also described the buildout's industrial reach. Natixis economists led by Alicia Garcia-Herrero estimated in a Monday note that global electricity demand from AI data centers would double over the next five years. They put China's share of global power-equipment exports at 33% last year, against 22% in 2017, and reported signs of renewed corporate capital spending in that industry. The finding identifies a potential beneficiary outside the frontier-model companies, with its growth outlook tied to supplying the physical infrastructure behind computing demand.

The IMF's Tuesday World Economic Outlook framed AI as a positive demand shock whose benefits had so far been concentrated in a relatively small group of economies, without yet lifting broad productivity. It raised its 2026 global growth forecast slightly to 3.1% and maintained 3.4% for 2027. A reassessment of expected profits and productivity could abruptly end that support, the fund warned, while depleted energy inventories narrowed the room for economies to absorb continuing disruption.

## Sovereign Refinancing Risks Reach Banks, Repos and Pension Funds

The IMF's new Global Financial Stability Report identified rising government bond yields as the largest emerging threat to the financial system. Athanasios Vamvakidis, deputy director of its capital-markets division, described the yield surge as the clearest change since April's assessment. The immediate concern was the combination of high debt, shorter maturities and more expensive refinancing, rather than inflation alone.

IMF official Jason Wu said rollover risks were greater because debt was larger and its maturity shorter. Price-sensitive investors, including hedge funds using bank leverage, also had a greater presence. Those characteristics can make a fiscal or inflation shock harder to absorb when borrowers must return frequently to markets. The fund's assessment of AI-correction risk was broadly unchanged from six months earlier: exceptionally strong earnings had eased valuation pressure, but leverage in the ecosystem had increased. Korea and Japan were among the equity markets most directly exposed.

France's supervisor offered a specific counterweight to concern about a sovereign-bank feedback loop. The ACPR reported Tuesday that French banks held about EUR190 billion of domestic public debt in 2025, representing 24% of their sovereign securities and 2% of total assets. Secretary general Emmanuelle Assouan said the diversified, limited exposure left the authority comfortable with the effect of recent spread moves, and that French banks held less domestic government debt than several European peers.

The authority had seen no automatic sovereign-downgrade triggers applied to French banks. Bloomberg Intelligence analysts nevertheless said negative action on the sovereign could pressure bank issuer and bond ratings. The supervisor's balance-sheet assessment and the ratings concern address different channels: the former concerns direct holdings and immediate resilience, while the latter concerns how a deterioration in national creditworthiness may affect lenders' funding standing.

Britain received a more favorable fiscal assessment from the IMF, conditional on continuing consolidation. The fund expects its deficit to fall from 3.8% of GDP this year to 1.4% in 2031, the largest projected reduction in the G7. Gross debt is forecast to rise from 102% this year to 102.5% in 2027 before declining to 100.2% in 2031. Separately, net debt was 93.8% in August, below earlier official projections around 100%; the gross and net measures describe different debt totals.

Retrospective upgrades to nominal output and inflation-supported tax receipts helped explain the better starting point. Oxford Economics' Andrew Goodwin cautioned that the expected path still involved debt rising before flattening because successive governments had scaled back tightening. The IMF urged Chancellor John Healey to make cost-of-living support targeted and temporary, avoiding broad fuel subsidies, generalized tax cuts and price controls that would be costly and difficult to withdraw.

Its UK growth forecast rose to 1.3% from 1% for 2026, while the 2027 estimate fell to 1.2% from 1.3%. The inflation projections of 3.3% this year and 2.8% next year assume Hormuz reopens in March and normal conditions return by the following October. That assumption places a concrete energy condition behind the outlook, while higher long-term rates are expected to restrain consumption and investment.

Ray Dalio presented a more bearish U.S. financing assessment in a Tuesday post. He estimated that the government would roll over about $10 trillion of obligations this year while adding $2.1 trillion of borrowing. Even a small reduction in reinvestment by existing holders could create a substantial gap, he argued. He also saw higher Japanese yields and incentives to support the yen as reasons domestic investors might repatriate some of their roughly $1.1 trillion in Treasuries. His warning concerns a potential supply-demand spiral over time, contrasting with the buyers supporting Tuesday's long-bond recovery.

Harley Bassman identified a different, technical vulnerability. As rising yields make longer-maturity securities cheapest to deliver into Treasury futures, the contracts acquire more duration and negative convexity. Managers seeking to offset that exposure may sell other long bonds as expiration approaches, amplifying an existing decline. Bassman said the negative convexity had reached levels last seen in 2007. He estimated that a 20-year yield above 6% could create selling equivalent to a $110 billion auction; the yield in his account was around 5.6%. The threshold describes a conditional risk, not selling realized Tuesday.

A newly released ICMA survey showed how European secured funding adapted during the first half of 2026. Voice brokers' share of outstanding repos reached 16.2% in June, about 2.5 percentage points higher than six months earlier and the largest since 2012. Electronic systems' share fell to 24.3%, a 16-year low. Across 60 respondents, repos and reverse repos totaled a record EUR14.92 trillion on June 10, up 9.3% from December.

Report author Richard Comotto said brokers could split large transactions and locate counterparties with less information leakage, particularly for irregular maturities or more difficult collateral. BrokerTec's Sara Carter said volatile conditions encouraged participants to shorten funding toward daily trades so positions could be unwound quickly. Repo rates were generally stable during the survey period despite volatility and quantitative tightening. In the UK, hedge funds' sales of long gilt positions were largely absorbed by real-money investors, reducing those positions' repo-financing needs. The historical survey documents a change in how liquidity was obtained rather than a new Tuesday funding-rate shock.

Chile's pension regulator disclosed a much larger consequence of the U.S. rates reversal. Foreign interest-rate derivatives held by the seven private AFP pension funds had swung from a $1.4 billion gain a year earlier to a $7.7 billion loss by September. The funds, managing about $229 billion, had built receiver-swap positions that benefited from falling U.S. rates. New derivative-risk limits taking effect November 4 now require further unwinding after higher yields made closing the contracts more expensive.

Citigroup estimated that by April the exposure had reached about $131 million for each basis-point yield move, compared with $10.6 million in early 2024. Contract notionals had fallen from a peak near $700 billion to about $525 billion in August. The regulator said a significant part of excess holdings had already been adjusted, although the remaining amount to unwind was unclear. The conservative E funds, which held most of the receiver positions, lost an average 10.4% this year, including 4.9% in September. C and D funds lost 3.1% and 4.2% that month. Declining exposure has therefore coexisted with a rising cost of exiting the remaining trades.

## Asian Policy Signals Diverge as Energy Costs Persist

Japan's new producer-price figures reduced the immediate urgency of another BOJ increase. Corporate goods prices rose 6.8% from a year earlier in September, slowing from 7.6%, and fell 0.3% month on month, matching August's decline. Agricultural, forestry and fishery prices dropped 13.3% year on year, led by rice, while petroleum and coal inflation slowed to 11.5% with help from subsidies. Input costs remained elevated, but their pace was easing.

People familiar with the BOJ's thinking said officials were leaning against a consecutive increase at the October 30 meeting, while keeping December open if the data warranted it. The board had raised rates to 1.25% in September. Tuesday's overnight-swaps pricing put the likelihood of an October increase at roughly 10%, with an 88% chance of a move by December. The account left the final October decision open if upside inflation risks increased abruptly.

Governor Kazuo Ueda told parliament Tuesday that the task was to stabilize underlying inflation around 2%. Officials will assess the effects of earlier tightening, elevated oil prices and a pending temporary food-sales-tax cut when preparing their quarterly outlook. Oil had risen about 15% since the late-July projections. The producer-price slowdown consequently supports more time to assess policy without removing the import-cost pressure facing Japan.

Australia's newly released September minutes gave a less patient explanation for the RBA's recent increase to 4.6%. Several upside risks identified in August had materialized or were building, and the board judged that waiting for confirmation could be costly. It questioned whether the previous 4.35% rate was sufficient to restore balance if the global neutral rate had risen. Relative interest-rate paths abroad also mattered through the exchange rate and imported inflation.

The minutes acknowledged a worsening tradeoff between returning inflation to the 2%-3% target and preserving employment. Persistent adverse supply shocks could require slower demand and job growth. The case for holding had centered on larger-than-expected downside risks, including the possibility that falling house prices would weaken household spending more than assumed. That distinction is important in an economy where housing prices had returned to year-earlier levels and confidence was deteriorating: the board chose to respond to inflation despite visible demand restraint.

Bank of Korea Governor Shin Hyun Song said Tuesday that policy would remain restrictive until officials were confident inflation would converge to target in a timely manner. He welcomed further won appreciation for its support to household purchasing power and the domestic economy. The benchmark is 3% following July and August increases, with further tightening intended to proceed gradually as their effects become clearer.

The IMF raised its 2026 Korean growth forecast by 0.7 percentage point to 3.3%, matching the BOK's own projection, and lifted its 2027 estimate to 2.8%. September exports more than doubled to a record $120.9 billion, with semiconductor shipments up 263%. Inflation eased to 2.9% from 3.1% in August but remained above the 2% target. Shin said AI demand was more than offsetting the war's drag on growth, while the two forces together intensified price pressure. He also said any review of the bank's six-month policy dot plot would follow at least a year of experience and occur next year or later, with no timetable fixed.

In Britain, BOE external member Megan Greene used the IMF's growth upgrade and signs of labor-market resilience to argue that the 3.75% policy rate was not restrictive enough. She has supported a quarter-point increase to 4% in recent months but remained in the minority on the nine-member MPC. Greene warned that repeated supply shocks could influence wage and price expectations, and argued that anticipated market tightening could reverse if the bank failed to deliver the increase priced by investors.

Bellway's results illustrated the constraint on housing demand alongside that argument. The builder expects 9,000-9,400 completions in the year through July 2027, down from 9,695, with average selling prices roughly flat at GBP325,000. Its underlying operating margin fell to 10.1%, and pretax profit of GBP270.2 million missed expectations. Chief financial officer Shane Doherty said rates of around 6% for first-time buyers were weighing on demand. The company's GBP150 million planned buyback accompanied, rather than removed, the weaker volume outlook.

Czech data added a distinct sign of broader inflation. September core inflation reached 3.1%, above the central bank's 2.9% forecast, with both market-services and goods prices accelerating slightly. Headline inflation rose to 2.5%, principally because of fuel, while falling food prices provided a smaller offset than before. Officials have said they will choose between holding and raising rates November 5; the central bank expects headline inflation temporarily to exceed 3% early in 2027.

Brazil moved in the opposite direction in economists' rate forecasts even as their inflation outlook worsened. The central bank's weekly survey lowered the year-end Selic estimate to 13.25% from 13.50%, against a current 13.75%, while raising expected year-end inflation to 5.22% from 5.01%. Investors were anticipating tighter fiscal policy under presidential challenger Flavio Bolsonaro. A Tuesday BTG Pactual/Nexus poll put him at 52% of valid votes against Lula's 48%, with a margin of error of 2 percentage points, ahead of the October 25 runoff. The lower rate forecast rests on a political expectation rather than an already-delivered fiscal adjustment.

## Credit Losses Expose Acquisition and Restructuring Risks

Skydance debt fell again Tuesday as investors reassessed profitability after its Warner Bros. Discovery acquisition. The 9.125% bonds due in 2036 dropped about 2.5 cents to 91 cents on the dollar, compared with their September 30 issue price of 100. Its investment-grade 7.55% notes due in 2033 widened to a 2.95-percentage-point risk premium from 2.87 on Friday and 2.375 at issuance. Five-year default protection rose to 5.728 percentage points from 5.132 on Friday.

JPMorgan research dated Tuesday quantified the deal's effect on new-issue performance. Over the 10 days through October 8, new investment-grade bonds underperformed the bank's broader index by 27 basis points, the largest gap since the pandemic. Excluding Skydance, new issues outperformed by about 4 basis points. The concentration of the loss helps explain why a poor aggregate new-issue result can coexist with firm demand for other transactions. The bank linked the weakness to issuance falling short of expectations despite strong fund inflows and lower rates volatility.

Altice International creditors took their asset-transfer dispute to court on October 13. A group including Arini, Diameter, Elliott, Silver Point, King Street, Sona and Invesco filed in New York state court, alleging a multi-year scheme to shift value beyond their reach with the involvement of controlling shareholder Patrick Drahi. The complaint identifies approximately $5.4 billion of intercompany loans moved to Altice Luxembourg, which is not obligated on the plaintiffs' debt, and loans to an entity holding Drahi's BT stake whose sale proceeds allegedly did not repay Altice International.

The creditors also challenge the November 2025 transfer of the Portuguese and Dominican businesses, which they say represented nearly 80% of adjusted EBITDA. The company has about EUR8 billion of net debt beginning to mature in 2027. It raised EUR750 million of new debt last year and created capacity for another EUR2 billion. The litigation follows talks last week and could complicate further financing that disadvantages the existing group. Altice and the creditors declined to comment; the asset-transfer claims are allegations in the lawsuit.

Senegal's effort to reach an IMF program and debt-relief agreement by year-end encountered a specific obstacle: an international audit of its liabilities remains outstanding, making board approval before year-end difficult, people familiar with the process said. A bondholder group including BlackRock, VR Capital and Farallon warned in an October 3 letter that demands for principal haircuts or lower average coupons could produce significant delays.

The group proposed extending eurobond maturities beyond the planned IMF program without nominal principal reductions or lower average coupons, arguing that this could satisfy comparability of treatment with official creditors. The IMF's debt-sustainability analysis will determine the required relief. Senegal's desired parallel negotiations with official and private lenders, its proposed exclusion of CFA franc debt and $1.7 billion of bank total-return swaps present additional issues for agreement.

The government's October 6 presentation put end-2025 debt at $48.4 billion, or 105% of rebased GDP, including $32.8 billion external debt. Commercial creditors were owed $9.7 billion and bilateral lenders $7.8 billion. Notes due in 2033 and 2048 traded just above 52 cents Tuesday, surrendering some gains following the presentation. The new audit constraint and creditor proposal narrow the practical route toward the intended December agreements and Q1 2027 implementation.

Uganda brought forward its own policy response by calling a special Wednesday meeting, rather than waiting until November 12. The shilling reached 4,224 per dollar Tuesday before recovering to 4,135 by late afternoon in Kampala. It had lost about 10% since August 25. Inflation reached 4.6% in September, its highest in more than three years, against a policy rate held at 9.75% since the previous meeting. Economist Ronald Ochen expected a rate increase in response to the exchange-rate pressure. The emergency meeting is the current change after the earlier investor withdrawals and presidential opposition to reserve sales.

New World's funding position acquired more detailed conditions in a fresh account of its late-September airport-property agreement. The Airport Authority will take over the HKD18 billion 11 Skies complex and waive billions in rent, while New World contributes HKD3 billion in cash and services. The authority can buy 750 million shares, about a 30% stake, from the Cheng family's investment arm within three years for HKD2.25 billion, roughly 43% below the current share price.

The option requires the family to remain the largest shareholder, creating a need for additional capital or an expanded equity base before exercise. People familiar with the discussions said the Chengs had recently considered a potential Bain investment but both sides had become more cautious amid macroeconomic uncertainty. The company faces nearly $11 billion of debt coming due as early as next year and has announced an exchange for about $991 million of 2027 and 2028 bonds. The agreement supplies time and liability relief, with the ownership condition shaping the next capital decision.

BP reported a contrasting balance-sheet improvement. Net debt fell to about $13.5 billion-$14.5 billion at the end of Q3 from $22.3 billion in June, reaching its end-2027 target range early. Refining margins were just below $47 a barrel and gas-trading earnings were significantly higher than in Q2, while oil trading was broadly flat. The company also disclosed $3 billion-$4.5 billion of impairments, largely in energy-transition businesses. Energy disruption was strengthening cash generation in refining and trading while exposing losses elsewhere in the portfolio.

Bank earnings showed another split in the higher-rate environment. JPMorgan, Citi and Wells Fargo set a fresh quarterly record for lending income as customers continued borrowing. Rates and spread-product trading softened, while currencies and commodities were more resilient; Citi was the exception to declining fixed-income revenue among the major banks reporting Tuesday. JPMorgan's equity-trading revenue rose 49% year on year. Across five large banks, equity revenues were on track for more than $66 billion in the first nine months, roughly $3 billion above expected bond, currency and commodity revenues, with the totals still including estimates for banks reporting Wednesday.

Later Tuesday coverage added institutional developments without changing the completed Treasury account. In a letter published after the 5 p.m. New York cutoff, Governor Lisa Cook's lawyer said she could not attend the November 5 White House hearing because of official European meetings and requested a date after the December 8-9 FOMC meeting. Cook denies the mortgage-fraud allegations and regards them as a pretext for removing her. Her lawyer questioned the investigation committee's objectivity, citing Kevin Hassett's public suggestion that there was cause to dismiss her.

A later KKR account offered a separate assessment of Asian credit valuations. Dengzhao Pan pointed to stronger balance sheets and lower expected credit losses at high-quality borrowers. Asian investment-grade dollar debt yielded an average 5.8%; it had lost about 1.4% this year, against 2.5% for U.S. peers, with average durations of 4.6 and 6.4 years respectively. Asian spreads were 15 basis points above early-June lows but still 2 basis points tighter than year-end 2025. That comparison distinguishes higher all-in yields from the much smaller change in credit compensation.

## Forward Market Significance

September U.S. CPI, due October 14 at 8:30 a.m. New York time, is the next direct test of the policy distinction Williams emphasized. Consensus expects headline inflation of 0.6% month on month after 0.4%, and 3.6% year on year after 3.4%. Core inflation is expected at 0.2% monthly after 0.3%, and 2.5% annually after 2.4%. Faster fuel inflation alongside moderating underlying prices would leave a different question from widening pressure across services and non-energy goods. The release is the last CPI before the October 27-28 FOMC meeting.

Wednesday's Beige Book will add regional business assessments. Thursday brings September PPI, expected to rise 0.5% after 0.4%, retail sales, expected at 0.3% after 1.2%, and initial claims, expected at 200,000 after 197,000. Friday's industrial-production consensus is a 0.4% increase after no change. Together, these observations will show whether the restraint visible in housing is becoming more widespread while demand associated with AI remains strong.

Singapore's Wednesday decision provides an earlier Asian policy test. Seventeen of 20 economists in Bloomberg's survey expect a steeper currency-policy-band slope and three expect no change. August core inflation of 2.2%, a two-year high, supports further restraint, while anticipated Q3 growth of 5.1% would mark a slowdown. Public-transport fares are scheduled to rise 7% in December, and Bank of America expects energy charges to rebound next year after declining this quarter. The issue is the persistence of imported inflation as growth moderates, not a conventional policy-rate decision.

Uganda's emergency meeting will reveal how the bank responds to the new currency extreme. Korea's October 22 decision and Japan's October 30 meeting face different combinations of strong technology demand and imported costs. Britain's October 28 budget will put the IMF's consolidation assessment beside Greene's concern about demand and inflation. Hungary's fiscal plan, expected next week, will give investors the next concrete numbers behind its euro-convergence ambition rather than another statement of the long-term goal.

Financing tests are becoming more issuer-specific. Senegal needs the liabilities audit and agreement on relief terms to sustain its year-end timetable; Chilean pension funds face the November 4 derivative limits after costly position reductions. Skydance's next trading and operating developments will matter to a new-issue market whose recent underperformance is unusually concentrated in that borrower. Meanwhile, renewed ship attacks around Hormuz and objections from Germany and Ukraine to a refinery-only energy truce keep physical fuel supply and the scope of any cessation of strikes unresolved. Those conditions remain consequential for the inflation outlook behind Wednesday's data and for borrowers refinancing at still-elevated yields.

overall_summary.headline: Long Treasuries rally as Williams sees no need for 2027 hikes under his forecast
overall_summary.session_narrative:
Longer Treasuries recovered as U.S. bond trading resumed after Monday's bank holiday. New York Fed President John Williams supported another rate increase this year but saw no need for further increases in 2027 if his forecast materializes, contrasting with futures pricing for a December increase and two more next year. Longer bonds had already found support from buying and expectations of reduced long-maturity Treasury supply before his remarks.

The 10-year yield fell 2.94 basis points to 5.2084% and the 30-year fell 3.87 basis points to 5.5569%, while the 2-year edged up 0.21 basis point to 4.789%. The 2s10s curve narrowed 3.15 basis points to 41.94. Most of the 10-year decline came from real yields, down 2.36 basis points to 2.8615%; breakeven inflation fell 0.58 basis point to 2.3469%. The weekly recovery still left 10-year and 30-year yields above their month-earlier levels.

Credit did not share the Treasury rally: U.S. investment-grade spreads widened modestly and high-yield spreads noticeably, while hard-currency EM spreads were little changed. Tencent completed almost $5.7 billion of bond financing, but AirTrunk delayed its planned $1.5 billion REIT listing amid higher rates and volatility. The IMF warned that larger sovereign debts, shorter maturities and leveraged investors were increasing refinancing vulnerability; Skydance's further debt losses exposed acquisition-specific pressure.

Equities recovered from session lows after Williams spoke, and the dollar weakened, but mixed oil moves left energy expensive. Wednesday's CPI will test whether inflation pressure remains concentrated in fuel or broadens into services and non-energy goods.
